nodes.label: Use tsvector for Full-Text Search
nodes.description: Use generated tsvector column + GIN index and to_tsquery/to_tsvector for full-text search instead of LIKE wildcard matching; supports ranking via ts_rank. ~100x faster than LIKE.

nodes.label: Index JSONB Columns for Efficient Querying
nodes.description: Use GIN indexes (jsonb_ops or jsonb_path_ops) for JSONB containment queries (@>, ?, ?&, ?|) and expression indexes for specific key lookups. 10-100x faster than unindexed JSONB scans.
nodes.norm_label: index jsonb columns for efficient querying

nodes.label: Configure Idle Connection Timeouts
nodes.description: Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and idle_session_timeout (and pgbouncer server/client_idle_timeout) to reclaim idle connection slots and release held locks. Reclaims 30-50% of slots.

nodes.label: Set Appropriate Connection Limits
nodes.description: Set max_connections based on RAM (each connection 1-3MB) and tune work_mem so work_mem*max_connections stays under 25% RAM; monitor via pg_stat_activity. Prevents OOM and crashes.

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.description: Use PgBouncer/connection pooler between app and Postgres; transaction mode returns connection after each transaction, session mode needed for prepared statements/temp tables. Handles 10-100x more concurrent users.
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications

nodes.label: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.description: Prepared statements bind to a connection; under transaction-mode pooling use unnamed prepared statements or deallocate after use, or use session-mode pooling (port 5432 vs 6543).
nodes.norm_label: use prepared statements correctly with pooling

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.description: Batch multiple rows into a single INSERT or use COPY for bulk loading instead of per-row inserts. 10-50x faster bulk inserts.
nodes.norm_label: batch insert statements for bulk data

nodes.label: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.description: Replace per-item loop queries with a single batched query using WHERE id = ANY(array[...]) or JOINs. 10-100x fewer round trips.
nodes.norm_label: eliminate n+1 queries with batch loading

nodes.label: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
nodes.description: Use keyset/cursor pagination (WHERE id > last_id) instead of OFFSET, which scans skipped rows; cursor pagination is O(1) regardless of page depth. Multi-column cursors must include all sort columns.
nodes.norm_label: use cursor-based pagination instead of offset

nodes.label: Use UPSERT for Insert-or-Update Operations
nodes.description: Use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT for atomic insert-or-update instead of check-then-insert, eliminating race conditions; supports DO NOTHING for insert-if-not-exists.

nodes.label: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
nodes.description: Use pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_xact_lock/pg_try_advisory_lock for app-level coordination instead of creating dummy rows to lock. Session-level or transaction-level, with non-blocking try-lock.
nodes.norm_label: use advisory locks for application-level locking

nodes.label: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.description: Acquire row locks in a consistent ID order (SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE) or use a single atomic UPDATE to prevent deadlocks. Monitor via pg_stat_database and log_lock_waits.
nodes.norm_label: prevent deadlocks with consistent lock ordering

nodes.label: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
nodes.description: Keep transactions minimal; do external API calls/validation outside the transaction and set statement_timeout to prevent runaway locks. 3-5x throughput, fewer deadlocks.
nodes.norm_label: keep transactions short to reduce lock contention

nodes.label: Use SKIP LOCKED for Non-Blocking Queue Processing
nodes.description: Use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (or atomic UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)) so multiple workers process distinct queue rows without blocking. ~10x throughput.
nodes.norm_label: use skip locked for non-blocking queue processing

nodes.label: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to Diagnose Slow Queries

nodes.label: Enable pg_stat_statements for Query Analysis
nodes.description: Enable pg_stat_statements extension to track per-query execution stats (calls, total/mean exec time) to find slowest and most frequent queries; reset after optimization.

nodes.label: Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE
nodes.description: Run ANALYZE (and VACUUM) to keep planner statistics fresh; tune autovacuum scale factors for high-churn tables; inspect via pg_stat_user_tables and pg_stat_progress_vacuum. 2-10x better plans.

nodes.label: Create Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries

nodes.label: Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries
nodes.summary: Use a single composite (multi-column) index instead of multiple single-column indexes for queries filtering on several columns. Column order matters: equality columns first, range columns last (leftmost prefix rule). Impact HIGH, 5-10x faster.

nodes.label: Covering Indexes (INCLUDE / Index-Only Scans)
nodes.summary: Use INCLUDE to add non-searchable SELECT columns to an index, enabling index-only scans that skip heap fetches. Impact MEDIUM-HIGH, 2-5x faster.

nodes.label: Choosing the Right Index Type (B-tree/GIN/GiST/BRIN/Hash)
nodes.summary: Default B-tree is not always optimal. GIN for arrays/JSONB/full-text, GiST for geometric/range/KNN, BRIN for large time-series (10-100x smaller), Hash for equality-only. Impact HIGH, 10-100x improvement.

nodes.label: Adding Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns
nodes.summary: Unindexed WHERE/JOIN columns cause full table scans that degrade exponentially with table growth. Index frequently filtered and foreign-key referencing columns. Impact CRITICAL, 100-1000x faster on large tables.
nodes.norm_label: adding indexes on where and join columns

nodes.label: Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries
nodes.summary: Partial indexes include only rows matching a WHERE condition, yielding smaller, faster indexes when queries consistently filter the same way (e.g. active users, pending orders). Impact HIGH, 5-20x smaller indexes.

nodes.label: Adding Constraints Safely in Migrations
nodes.summary: Postgres lacks ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS; use a DO block checking pg_constraint for idempotent migrations. Applies to unique, check, and foreign-key constraints. Impact HIGH.

nodes.label: Choosing Appropriate Data Types
nodes.summary: Use bigint (not int) IDs, text (not varchar(n)), timestamptz (not timestamp), numeric (not float) for money, and text+check or enum types. Impact HIGH, 50% storage reduction.

nodes.label: Indexing Foreign Key Columns
nodes.summary: Postgres does not auto-index FK columns; missing indexes slow JOINs and ON DELETE CASCADE. Always index the referencing column. Includes diagnostic query for missing FK indexes. Impact HIGH, 10-100x faster.

nodes.label: Lowercase Identifiers for Compatibility
nodes.summary: Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase; quoted mixed-case breaks ORMs/tools/AI assistants. Use lowercase snake_case; create views as compatibility layers when stuck. Impact MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Partitioning Large Tables
nodes.summary: Partition large (100M+ row, time-series) tables by range (e.g. monthly) to speed queries and enable instant old-data drops. Impact MEDIUM-HIGH, 5-20x faster.

nodes.label: Optimal Primary Key Strategy
nodes.summary: Use bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY for single DB; UUIDv7 or ULID for distributed time-ordered IDs. Avoid random UUIDv4 (index fragmentation); identity preferred over serial. Impact HIGH.

nodes.label: Principle of Least Privilege (Roles & Grants)
nodes.summary: Grant minimal specific privileges; never use superuser for app queries. Use nologin roles (app_readonly/app_writer) and revoke public defaults to reduce attack surface. Impact MEDIUM.

nodes.label: Row Level Security Basics

nodes.label: supabase-postgres-best-practices skill
nodes.description: Kiro skill providing Postgres performance optimization and best-practice reference docs, organized into sections by filename prefix.

nodes.label: Section: Query Performance (query)
nodes.description: CRITICAL section: slow queries, missing indexes, inefficient query plans. Most common source of Postgres performance issues.

nodes.label: Section: Connection Management (conn)
nodes.description: CRITICAL section: connection pooling, limits, serverless strategies. Critical for high concurrency or serverless deployments.

nodes.label: Section: Concurrency & Locking (lock)
nodes.description: MEDIUM-HIGH section: transaction management, isolation levels, deadlock prevention, lock contention.

nodes.label: Section: Data Access Patterns (data)
nodes.description: MEDIUM section: N+1 elimination, batch operations, cursor pagination, efficient data fetching.

nodes.label: Section: Monitoring & Diagnostics (monitor)
nodes.description: LOW-MEDIUM section: pg_stat_statements, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, metrics collection, performance diagnostics.

nodes.label: Section: Advanced Features (advanced)
nodes.description: LOW section: full-text search, JSONB optimization, PostGIS, extensions, advanced features.

nodes.label: Writing Guidelines for Postgres References
nodes.description: Meta-doc: how to author effective AI-agent-friendly Postgres reference docs. Concrete transformation patterns, error-first structure, quantified impact, self-contained examples, semantic naming, impact levels, review checklist.

nodes.label: Section Definitions
nodes.description: Meta-doc: defines rule categories (sections) for Postgres best practices; rules auto-assigned by filename prefix.

nodes.label: Reference Template
nodes.description: Meta-doc: front-matter + Incorrect/Correct SQL example template for authoring a Postgres best-practice reference.

nodes.label: Use tsvector for Full-Text Search
nodes.description: Replaces LIKE wildcards (unindexable) with generated tsvector column + GIN index + to_tsquery; ~100x faster with ranking support (ts_rank).

nodes.label: Index JSONB Columns for Efficient Querying
nodes.description: GIN index for JSONB containment (@>, ?, ?&, ?|); expression index for key lookups; jsonb_path_ops class is 2-3x smaller. 10-100x faster JSONB queries.
nodes.norm_label: index jsonb columns for efficient querying

nodes.label: Configure Idle Connection Timeouts
nodes.description: Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and idle_session_timeout to reclaim 30-50% of connection slots; also configure pgbouncer server_idle_timeout / client_idle_timeout.

nodes.label: Set Appropriate Connection Limits
nodes.description: Each connection uses 1-3MB RAM; set max_connections based on RAM and work_mem * max_connections <= 25% RAM to prevent OOM crashes.

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.description: PgBouncer between app and DB; pool_size = (CPU cores * 2) + spindle_count; transaction mode vs session mode. Handles 10-100x more concurrent users.
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications

nodes.label: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.description: Named prepared statements conflict in transaction-mode pooling (port 6543); use unnamed statements, deallocate after use, or session mode (port 5432).
nodes.norm_label: use prepared statements correctly with pooling

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.description: Multi-row INSERT values or COPY for bulk loading; 10-50x faster than individual inserts (one round trip per ~1000 rows).
nodes.norm_label: batch insert statements for bulk data

nodes.label: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.description: Replace per-item loop queries with WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[]) or JOIN; 10-100x fewer round trips.
nodes.norm_label: eliminate n+1 queries with batch loading

nodes.label: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
nodes.description: WHERE id > last_id keyset pagination is O(1) vs OFFSET which rescan skipped rows; multi-column cursors use (col, id) > (val, val).
nodes.norm_label: use cursor-based pagination instead of offset

nodes.label: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
nodes.description: pg_advisory_lock / pg_advisory_xact_lock / pg_try_advisory_lock for coordination without locking real rows; no row-level lock overhead.
nodes.norm_label: use advisory locks for application-level locking

nodes.label: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.description: Acquire locks in consistent ID order (SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE) or single atomic UPDATE; set log_lock_waits / deadlock_timeout to detect.
nodes.norm_label: prevent deadlocks with consistent lock ordering

nodes.label: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
nodes.description: Move external API calls outside transaction; hold lock only for actual update; use statement_timeout. 3-5x throughput improvement.
nodes.norm_label: keep transactions short to reduce lock contention

nodes.label: Use SKIP LOCKED for Non-Blocking Queue Processing
nodes.description: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lets parallel workers claim distinct queue rows without waiting; 10x throughput for worker queues.
nodes.norm_label: use skip locked for non-blocking queue processing

nodes.label: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to Diagnose Slow Queries
nodes.description: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) reveals true timings; look for Seq Scan on large tables, Rows Removed by Filter, read>>hit buffers, external merge sorts.
nodes.norm_label: use explain analyze to diagnose slow queries

nodes.label: Enable pg_stat_statements for Query Analysis
nodes.description: Extension tracking per-query exec stats; rank by total_exec_time / calls / mean_exec_time > 100ms to find top resource-consuming queries.

nodes.label: Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE
nodes.description: ANALYZE refreshes planner statistics (2-10x better plans); tune autovacuum scale factors for high-churn tables; check pg_stat_progress_vacuum.
nodes.norm_label: maintain table statistics with vacuum and analyze

nodes.label: Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries
nodes.summary: Use a single composite (multi-column) B-tree index instead of separate single-column indexes for queries filtering on multiple columns. Place equality columns first and range columns last (leftmost-prefix rule); supports 5-10x faster multi-column queries.

nodes.label: Covering Indexes to Avoid Table Lookups
nodes.summary: Use INCLUDE for columns selected but not filtered on, enabling index-only scans that skip the heap. 2-5x faster queries by eliminating table fetches.
nodes.norm_label: covering indexes to avoid table lookups

nodes.label: Add Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns
nodes.summary: Filtering or joining on unindexed columns causes full sequential scans that worsen exponentially with table growth. Index frequently filtered columns and the foreign-key side of JOINs. 100-1000x faster queries on large tables.
nodes.norm_label: add indexes on where and join columns

nodes.label: Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries
nodes.summary: Partial indexes include only rows matching a WHERE clause (e.g., deleted_at is null, status='pending', sku is not null), making them smaller and faster when queries consistently filter the same condition. 5-20x smaller indexes, faster writes and queries.

nodes.label: Add Constraints Safely in Migrations
nodes.summary: PostgreSQL has no ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS; use a DO block querying pg_constraint (contype p/f/u/c) to create unique, check, and foreign-key constraints idempotently in migrations.

nodes.label: Index Foreign Key Columns
nodes.summary: Postgres does not auto-index FK columns; missing indexes slow JOINs and ON DELETE CASCADE. Always index the FK referencing column. A pg_constraint/pg_index query finds missing FK indexes. 10-100x faster JOINs and CASCADE.

nodes.label: Select Optimal Primary Key Strategy
nodes.summary: PK choice affects insert performance, index size, replication. Prefer bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY; for distributed, use UUIDv7 (pg_uuidv7) or time-prefixed IDs. Avoid random UUIDv4 (index fragmentation) on large tables. 'serial' works but identity is SQL-standard.
